popCulture.title: Orpheus
popCulture.description: Oeagrus is the Thracian king (or wine-hero) most often named as Orpheus' father by Calliope — the mortal stem of the singer who moved the underworld.

popCulture.title: Oeagrus
popCulture.description: King of Thrace, husband of Calliope, father of Orpheus and (in some accounts) Linus — the Oeagrides as a byname of the Muses.

popCulture.title: Calliope
popCulture.description: The Muse of epic song is Oeagrus' consort in the standard Orphic genealogy — Apollo sometimes named instead as Orpheus' father.

popCulture.title: Dionysiaca
popCulture.creator: Nonnus
popCulture.description: Nonnus brings Oeagrus into Dionysus' Indian war as a harper and father of Orpheus — late epic keeping the Thracian king on the god's campaign.
